items.stem: During a busy shift, a nurse notices a colleague is overloaded with tasks while a stable client’s care is delayed. Using TeamSTEPPS mutual support (task assistance), which action best fits the model?

options.text: Offer help in the context of patient safety (for example, “I have 10 minutes—how can I help?”) and assist as appropriate
Ignore the overload so the colleague ‘learns resilience’ without assistance
Publicly criticize the colleague for poor time management in front of the client
Leave the unit without notifying anyone so the colleague has fewer people to manage

rationales.A: Correct. AHRQ TeamSTEPPS mutual support (task assistance): foster a climate where assistance is sought and offered; place offers/requests in the context of patient safety; asking “I have 10 minutes. How can I help?” strengthens team resilience. OpenStax: mutual support means knowing team member needs and taking steps to meet them.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Mutual support expects assistance to be actively sought and offered to protect from work overload (AHRQ).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Formative/supportive teamwork focuses on behaviours and safety, not public personal criticism (AHRQ feedback principles).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Abandoning the unit worsens safety and is not mutual support.

items.stem: A charge nurse reviews TeamSTEPPS with new staff. Complete the teaching statement.

ngn.template: TeamSTEPPS core skills include team leadership, communication, {B1}, and {B2} (also called backup behaviour), which involves assisting teammates and advocating when safety is threatened.

rationales.B1a: Correct. OpenStax and AHRQ: situation monitoring is a TeamSTEPPS core competency/skill.
rationales.B1b: Incorrect. Punitive silence is not a TeamSTEPPS skill.
rationales.B1c: Incorrect. TeamSTEPPS emphasizes shared situation awareness, not unilateral unshared decisions.
rationales.B2a: Correct. AHRQ: mutual support (backup behaviour) includes assisting teammates and assertive advocacy for safety. OpenStax lists mutual support as a core competency.
rationales.B2b: Incorrect. Mutual support addresses workload and assistance rather than ignoring overload.
rationales.B2c: Incorrect. Advocacy/assertion is part of mutual support, not withholding concerns.

items.stem: A community health nurse teaches adults how to prevent hepatitis A. Which instructions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hepatitis A vaccination is the best way to prevent infection
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after using the bathroom, after caring for someone who is ill, after changing diapers, and before preparing or eating food
Practise good personal hygiene and food/water safety to reduce fecal–oral transmission
Rely on isolation of infected persons as the primary community prevention strategy because hygiene and vaccine add little
International travelers and other higher-risk groups should discuss hepatitis A vaccination with a clinician

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: vaccination is the best way to prevent hepatitis A.
rationales.B: Correct. CDC: good hand hygiene with soap and water at key times helps prevent spread.
rationales.C: Correct. Merck: good personal hygiene and food/water safety help prevent fecal–oral transmission.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Merck: isolation does little to prevent HAV spread; hygiene/vaccine are the prevention focus.
rationales.E: Correct. CDC and Merck list international travelers and other higher-risk groups among those recommended for vaccination.

items.stem: An 82-year-old client living in a retirement residence develops new confusion over 12 hours without reported dysuria. Which nursing interpretation is most accurate?

options.text: Acute confusion in an older adult can be an atypical presentation of urinary tract infection and warrants prompt clinical evaluation (including urine testing as indicated)
New delirium in older adults is almost never related to infection, so infection workup can be deferred indefinitely
UTI in older adults always presents with classic dysuria and frequency, so absent dysuria rules out UTI
Confusion should be attributed only to dementia progression without assessing acute medical causes

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: older adults may present with sepsis and delirium without urinary-tract symptoms. OpenStax: older adults’ UTIs often present atypically with confusion/delirium; OpenStax delirium text notes UTI as a common cause and that older adults may lack pain.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Infection (including UTI) is a common precipitant of delirium (Merck Delirium etiology; OpenStax).
rationales.C: Incorrect. OpenStax and Merck emphasize atypical presentations without classic dysuria.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Acute confusion requires evaluation for reversible causes such as infection (OpenStax/Merck).

items.stem: A client arrives after prolonged outdoor cold exposure with a numb, pale finger. Which initial rewarming approach is most appropriate if medical care is arranged and refreezing will not occur?

options.text: Immerse the frostbitten area in warm (about 37–39 °C / warm-to-touch, not hot) water; do not rub or massage the area
Rub snow vigorously onto the finger to ‘restore circulation’
Place the numb finger directly on a stove burner or heating pad for rapid dry heat
Ignore the finding because numbness means tissue injury cannot occur

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: rewarm by immersion in 37–39 °C water; avoid rubbing. CDC: place frostbitten areas in warm-to-touch (not hot) water; do not rub/massage; avoid heating pads/stoves.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CDC/Merck: do not rub or massage frostbitten tissue (worsens injury).
rationales.C: Incorrect. CDC/Merck: avoid uncontrolled dry heat (stove, heating pad) because numbness risks burns.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Numbness is a classic frostbite finding and needs care (CDC/Merck).

items.stem: A hiker has a cold, numb, white fingertip after hours in sub-freezing wind. Complete the bowtie: most likely condition, two priority actions, and two monitoring parameters.

conditions.text: Isolated anxiety attack without cold exposure

actions.text: Move to a warm shelter and arrange prompt medical evaluation
Rewarm the affected part in warm (≈37–39 °C / warm-to-touch) water without rubbing
Massage the area firmly with snow to restore colour
Apply a heating pad directly to the numb skin for rapid dry heat
Encourage prolonged walking on frostbitten feet to ‘work out’ stiffness

parameters.text: Colour, sensation, and pain response of the rewarming digit
Signs of concurrent hypothermia (confusion, shivering, drowsiness)
Daily pollen count as the primary outcome
Core temperature trending above 40 °C as the expected goal
Ability to complete a marathon within 1 hour

rationales.K1: Correct. Cold, numb, white distal tissue after freezing exposure fits frostbite (Merck/CDC).
rationales.K2: Incorrect. Allergic rhinitis does not explain freezing tissue injury.
rationales.K3: Incorrect. Heatstroke is heat illness, not freezing injury.
rationales.K4: Incorrect. History is cold exposure with tissue findings.
rationales.A1: Correct. CDC: seek medical attention; get into a warm room/shelter.
rationales.A2: Correct. Merck/CDC: warm-water rewarming; do not rub.
rationales.A3: Incorrect. Do not rub/massage or use snow (CDC/Merck).
rationales.A4: Incorrect. Avoid heating pads/dry heat on numb tissue (CDC/Merck).
rationales.A5: Incorrect. CDC: avoid walking on frostbitten feet/toes unless necessary.
rationales.P1: Correct. Clinical course after rewarming includes colour/pain/edema changes (Merck).
rationales.P2: Correct. CDC: check for hypothermia, which is a more serious emergency.
rationales.P4: Incorrect. >40 °C is heatstroke territory, not frostbite goal.
rationales.P5: Incorrect. Not a frostbite monitoring parameter.

items.stem: A client with known primary adrenal insufficiency develops vomiting, abdominal pain, and hypotension after a gastrointestinal illness. Which action is the immediate priority?

options.text: Recognize possible adrenal crisis and ensure emergency glucocorticoid therapy (e.g., IV hydrocortisone) with fluid resuscitation is instituted without delay
Withhold all steroids indefinitely because illness means hormones are unnecessary
Focus only on outpatient scheduling of elective imaging before any hormone replacement
Give a large dose of insulin as first-line therapy for adrenal crisis

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: institute therapy immediately on suspicion of adrenal crisis; delay in glucocorticoid therapy may be fatal; hydrocortisone IV and volume expansion. OpenStax: adrenal crisis treated with IV fluids, dextrose, and hydrocortisone; emergency—notify provider immediately.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Illness/stress increases glucocorticoid need; abrupt inadequate dosing precipitates crisis (OpenStax/Merck).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Emergency hormone/fluid therapy precedes elective diagnostics (Merck: do not delay treatment).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Insulin is not first-line adrenal crisis therapy; hydrocortisone and fluids are.

items.stem: A client with central diabetes insipidus (arginine vasopressin deficiency) has massive polyuria. Which medication teaching is most accurate?

options.text: Desmopressin (a vasopressin analogue) is used to replace antidiuretic activity and reduce polyuria
Desmopressin is used primarily to raise blood glucose in diabetic ketoacidosis
No hormone replacement exists; only lifelong fluid restriction without medication is used for complete central DI
Desmopressin is an antibiotic taken to sterilize the urinary tract in DI

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: desmopressin is the synthetic vasopressin analogue used for hormonal treatment of arginine vasopressin deficiency. OpenStax: desmopressin replaces vasopressin and acts as an antidiuretic to treat polyuria.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Desmopressin is not a DKA glucose therapy.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Hormone replacement with desmopressin is standard (Merck/OpenStax).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Desmopressin is not an antibiotic.

items.stem: A clinic implements a trauma-informed approach. Which organizational priority best reflects a core trauma-informed principle?

options.text: Ensure participants and staff feel physically and psychologically safe, and structure care to avoid re-traumatization
Maximize unpredictable loud announcements and crowded, poorly lit waiting areas to ‘desensitize’ clients
Ignore power dynamics and withhold collaboration because clients should not share decisions
Use seclusion as the first response to mild anxiety without attempting less restrictive supports

rationales.A: Correct. SAMHSA: Safety—participants and staff feel physically and psychologically safe. OpenStax: creating a safe environment is a top priority; avoid re-traumatization.
rationales.B: Incorrect. OpenStax emphasizes good lighting, reduced noise/distractions, and welcoming environments for safety.
rationales.C: Incorrect. SAMHSA principles include collaboration/mutuality and empowerment, not withholding collaboration.
rationales.D: Incorrect. SAMHSA materials emphasize eliminating harmful seclusion/restraint practices; safety supports come first.

items.stem: A nurse teaches an older adult who walks outdoors in winter how to reduce frostbite risk. Which instruction is best?

options.text: Cover commonly affected areas (nose, ears, cheeks, chin, fingers, toes) with warm, dry clothing such as a hat, scarf/mask, mittens, and layered loose clothing; limit prolonged outdoor exposure in extreme cold
Wear a single thin damp cotton layer and leave ears and fingers uncovered to ‘toughen’ the skin
Rub snow on exposed skin every few minutes as primary prevention
Stay outdoors longer when numb because numbness means protection is complete

rationales.A: Correct. CDC winter guidance: cover nose/ears/toes/cheeks/chin/fingers; hat, mittens, layered loose clothing; limit extreme cold exposure. Merck: distal extremities and exposed skin are most often affected.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CDC emphasizes covering high-risk areas and proper layered dry clothing.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Rubbing snow is harmful for frostbite care and is not prevention (CDC).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Numbness is a frostbite warning sign, not reassurance (CDC/Merck).

items.stem: A public health nurse prepares winter safety messaging. Which points are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: When possible, limit outdoor time during extreme cold and dress in several layers of loose-fitting clothing
Cover ears, nose, cheeks, chin, fingers, and toes with warm dry clothing
Check on older adults who may have inadequate heating, food, or clothing
Treat numbness of fingers after freezing exposure by vigorous massage with snow
Seek medical care for suspected frostbite and watch for hypothermia warning signs such as confusion or drowsiness

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: stay indoors if possible in extreme cold; wear several layers of loose-fitting clothing.
rationales.B: Correct. CDC: cover body parts most often affected by frostbite.
rationales.C: Correct. CDC: older adults with inadequate food, clothing, or heating are at higher hypothermia risk.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CDC: do not rub or massage frostbitten areas; do not use snow.
rationales.E: Correct. CDC: seek medical care for frostbite; hypothermia signs include confusion and drowsiness.
